claims.law_text:
/-- "Return ``(price_in, price_out)`` from the Puppetmaster registry, or zeros."
The output is zeros, or the two prices of one registry row. -/
def FromRegistryOrZeros (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x →
    f x = zeros ∨
      ∃ s ∈ x.registry,
        priceValue s.inputPerMtok = some (priceIn (f x)) ∧
        priceValue s.outputPerMtok = some (priceOut (f x))

/-- "Return ``(price_in, price_out)`` from the Puppetmaster registry, or zeros."
If the registry has one row, and its id is exactly the non-empty `model_id`,
and both of its prices are positive integers, the row prices the model.
The output is the two prices of the row (the owner accepted `5 5` for a row
with id `a` and prices 5 and 5, even if it has no adapter model name). -/
def ExactIdRowPriced (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → ∀ s : Spec, x.registry = [s] →
    x.modelId ≠ [] → s.id = some x.modelId →
    ∀ a b : Int, 0 < a → 0 < b →
      s.inputPerMtok = .num a → s.outputPerMtok = .num b →
      f x = (a, b)

/-- "Return ``(price_in, price_out)`` from the Puppetmaster registry, or zeros."
The output is the zero pair, or the rate pair of one registry row. -/
def FromRegistryOrZeros (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x →
    f x = zeroRates ∨
      ∃ s ∈ x.registry,
        priceValue s.inputPrice = some (f x).priceIn ∧
        priceValue s.outputPrice = some (f x).priceOut

/-- "Return the shared positive rate pair, or ``(0, 0)`` when rates conflict."
A non-zero output is the rate pair of a registry row with a positive input rate. -/
def NonzeroIsPositivePair (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → f x ≠ zeroRates →
    ∃ s ∈ x.registry,
      positiveInput s = true ∧
      priceValue s.inputPrice = some (f x).priceIn ∧
      priceValue s.outputPrice = some (f x).priceOut

/-- A row is priced only when it matches the model id. A non-zero output comes
from a row with an id that relates to `model_id`. A row whose ids have nothing
in common with `model_id` gives no rate. -/
def NonzeroFromMatchingRow (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → f x ≠ zeroRates →
    ∃ s ∈ x.registry,
      (∃ i ∈ rowIds s, idRelated x.modelId i) ∧
      priceValue s.inputPrice = some (f x).priceIn ∧
      (priceValue s.outputPrice = some (f x).priceOut ∨ (f x).priceOut = 0)

/-- "Only a cumulative snapshot is absorbed: ``incoming`` starts with the whole
``accumulated`` text." A call whose ``incoming`` does not start with
``accumulated`` returns the whole ``incoming`` text: nothing is dropped. -/
def NonCumulativeKept (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → cumulative x = false → f x = incText x

/-- "Only a cumulative snapshot is absorbed: ``incoming`` starts with the whole
``accumulated`` text." A call whose ``incoming`` does not start with
``accumulated`` returns the whole ``incoming`` text, unless ``incoming`` after
its leading whitespace starts with ``accumulated``. Then the law says nothing. -/
def NonCumulativeKept (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → cumulative x = false →
    (accText x).isPrefixOf ((incText x).dropWhile isPyWs) = false → f x = incText x

/-- "Return the new suffix to append". When ``incoming`` starts with ``accumulated``,
``accumulated`` has at least the floor length, and the new part has a non-whitespace
character, the call returns the part of ``incoming`` after ``accumulated``. -/
def SnapshotSuffix (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → cumulative x = true → longAcc x = true →
    blank (rest x) = false → f x = rest x

/-- "Snapshot floor: a \"snapshot\" of fewer chars than this is just a short delta."
When ``accumulated`` is shorter than the floor, the call returns the whole
``incoming`` text. -/
def ShortAccKept (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → longAcc x = false → f x = incText x

/-- "Return the new suffix to append". When ``incoming`` starts with ``accumulated``,
``accumulated`` has at least the floor length, ``accumulated`` is not one repeated
character, and the new part has a non-whitespace character, the call returns the part of
``incoming`` after ``accumulated``. A repeated character is not a snapshot (sentence 9),
and the owner accepts the empty output for ``a`` then ``aa``. -/
def SnapshotSuffix (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → cumulative x = true → longAcc x = true →
    (∀ c ∈ accText x, c = (accText x).headD ' ') = false →
    blank (rest x) = false → f x = rest x

/-- "Return the new suffix to append". When ``incoming`` starts with ``accumulated``,
``accumulated`` has at least the floor length, ``accumulated`` is not one repeated
character, the new part has a non-whitespace character, and the new part is not a copy
of ``accumulated``, the call returns the part of ``incoming`` after ``accumulated``.
A repeated character is not a snapshot (sentence 9), and the owner accepts the empty
output for ``a`` then ``aa``. A new part equal to ``accumulated`` is message+message
(sentence 2), and the owner accepts the empty output for ``ab`` then ``abab``. -/
def SnapshotSuffix (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → cumulative x = true → longAcc x = true →
    (∀ c ∈ accText x, c = (accText x).headD ' ') = false →
    blank (rest x) = false → rest x ≠ accText x → f x = rest x

/-- "Concrete path:line from a structured status row's own evidence only."
A lone settled row whose evidence is any plain `dir/name.ext:line` settles its normalized key at
that evidence, not only `src/a.py:12`. -/
def SettledRowYieldsItsOwnLocus (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, Legal x → ∀ r : Fields,
    x.criteria = some [Item.dict r] →
    criterionKey r ≠ "" →
    isVerifyStatus r = true →

    (f x).lookup (criterionKey r) = some (evidenceText r)

/-- "The (CAP+1)th identical call hard-suppresses with the existing error".
A call that already ran the cap number of times is hard suppressed (a wait and
a command with a changed context are not repeats of this kind). A live browser
observation is not a repeat of this kind: the owner confirmed that the guard
does not suppress it at the cap. -/
def CapHardSuppresses (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → guardEnabled x = true → x.query.kind ≠ "wait" →
    isBrowserObservation x.query = false →
    staleCommand x = false → loopRepeatCap ≤ priorCount x →
    (f x).suppress = true ∧ (f x).reason = Reason.loop ∧ (f x).replay = false

/-- "The (CAP+1)th identical call hard-suppresses with the existing error".
A call that already ran the cap number of times is hard suppressed (a wait and
a command with a changed context are not repeats of this kind). A live browser
observation is not a repeat of this kind: the owner confirmed that the guard
does not suppress it at the cap. The same holds for a computer_use observation
(status, apps, snapshot): the owner confirmed the guard lets it run. -/
def CapHardSuppresses (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → guardEnabled x = true → x.query.kind ≠ "wait" →
    isBrowserObservation x.query = false → isComputerObservation x.query = false →
    staleCommand x = false → loopRepeatCap ≤ priorCount x →
    (f x).suppress = true ∧ (f x).reason = Reason.loop ∧ (f x).replay = false

/-- "a session missing from the CLI's local store": when the local store folder of
the adapter exists, a resolved record names a session that has a file in it. An
absent folder does not block a resolved record. -/
def ResolvedNeedsLocalStore (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → isResolved (f x) = true →
    (∀ ids s, resolvedAdapter (f x) = some "codex" → x.codexDisk = some ids →
      resolvedSession (f x) = some s → s ∈ ids) ∧
    (∀ ids s, resolvedAdapter (f x) = some "claude-code" → x.claudeDisk = some ids →
      resolvedSession (f x) = some s → s ∈ ids)

/-- "a session missing from the CLI's local store": when the local store folder of
the adapter exists, a resolved record names a session that has a file in it. An
absent folder does not block a resolved record. An id that the caller gave itself
(`resume_session_id`) is not checked against the folder: the law covers a session that
comes from a `resume_from` receipt only. -/
def ResolvedNeedsLocalStore (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → x.resumeFrom ≠ ResumeFrom.none → explicitSession x = "" →
    isResolved (f x) = true →
    (∀ ids s, resolvedAdapter (f x) = some "codex" → x.codexDisk = some ids →
      resolvedSession (f x) = some s → s ∈ ids) ∧
    (∀ ids s, resolvedAdapter (f x) = some "claude-code" → x.claudeDisk = some ids →
      resolvedSession (f x) = some s → s ∈ ids)

/-- "`resume_session_id` (an id the caller kept itself)" and "continue a prior codex or
claude-code worker's provider session": with no `resume_from`, a valid explicit session id,
a resumable task adapter and no `resume_adapter`, the request resolves. The record names the
task adapter and the given id, and it has no source job or task. It needs no store. -/
def ExplicitSessionResolves (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → x.resumeFrom = ResumeFrom.none → validSessionId (explicitSession x) = true →
    resumable x.adapter = true → x.resumeAdapter = none →
    f x = Output.resolved x.adapter (explicitSession x) none none

/-- "`resume_session_id` (an id the caller kept itself)" and "continue a prior codex or
claude-code worker's provider session": with no `resume_from`, a valid explicit session id,
a resumable task adapter, no `resume_adapter` and a store, the request resolves. The record names the
task adapter and the given id, and it has no source job or task. With no store (`store = none`)
the shipped code answers unavailable, so the law does not cover that case. -/
def ExplicitSessionResolves (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → x.resumeFrom = ResumeFrom.none → validSessionId (explicitSession x) = true →
    resumable x.adapter = true → x.resumeAdapter = none → x.store ≠ none →
    f x = Output.resolved x.adapter (explicitSession x) none none

/-- "True when the user asked to launch a swarm, not merely mentioned one."
A message that has neither the word `swarm` nor the word `worker` (in any
letter case) asks for no swarm, so it is not an explicit swarm message. -/
def NoSwarmWordNotSwarm (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x →
    ¬ ("swarm".toList <:+: lowerWord x.message) →
    ¬ ("worker".toList <:+: lowerWord x.message) → f x = false

/-- "True when the user asked to launch a swarm, not merely mentioned one."
A message that has neither the word `swarm` nor the word `worker` (in any
letter case) and not the word `fanout` asks for no swarm, so it is not an
explicit swarm message. The message `fanout` is an explicit swarm message. -/
def NoSwarmWordNotSwarm (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x →
    ¬ ("swarm".toList <:+: lowerWord x.message) →
    ¬ ("worker".toList <:+: lowerWord x.message) →
    ¬ ("fanout".toList <:+: lowerWord x.message) → f x = false

/-- "True when the user asked to launch a swarm, not merely mentioned one."
A message that has neither the word `swarm` nor the word `worker` (in any
letter case) and not the word `fanout` or `fan-out` asks for no swarm, so it is
not an explicit swarm message. -/
def NoSwarmWordNotSwarm (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x →
    ¬ ("swarm".toList <:+: lowerWord x.message) →
    ¬ ("worker".toList <:+: lowerWord x.message) →
    ¬ ("fanout".toList <:+: lowerWord x.message) →
    ¬ ("fan-out".toList <:+: lowerWord x.message) → f x = false

/-- "Scan run_command events ..." Only the text that `eventCommand` returns is
scanned. Every reported destination is the normal form of a path token (a run
of characters with no path stop character, after a `/`) in the command of some
event. A text in the event that is not its command gives no destination. -/
def SourcedFromCommand (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → ∀ p ∈ f x,
    ∃ (e : Event) (c pre s post : List Char),
      e ∈ x.events ∧ eventCommand e = some c ∧
      c = pre ++ '/' :: s ++ post ∧ (∀ ch ∈ s, isPathStop ch = false) ∧
      p = candidateNorm ('/' :: s)

/-- "Adapters that can actually modify the working tree." /
"_EDIT_CAPABLE_ADAPTERS = frozenset({"agentic", "claude-code", "codex"})":
only an edit-capable adapter can leave file changes behind. -/
def OnlyEditCapable (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → f x = true → isEditCapable x.adapter = true

/-- "Adapters that can actually modify the working tree." /
"_EDIT_CAPABLE_ADAPTERS = frozenset({"agentic", "claude-code", "codex"})":
only an edit-capable adapter can leave file changes behind. The owner
confirmed one exception: an empty adapter with an implement request
(`mode=implement` or truthy `implement`) can give true. -/
def OnlyEditCapable (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → f x = true →
    isEditCapable x.adapter = true ∨ (x.adapter = [] ∧ asksImplement (payloadOf x) = true)

/-- "'provider:model'  -> explicit provider + model (e.g. 'anthropic:claude-opus-4-8')"
A spec with a colon whose provider part names a provider in the table gives a
driver for that provider, with the part after the colon as the model.
Also: "candidate API-key env vars, first match wins" (the key variable). -/
def ExplicitProviderModel (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → hasColon x.spec = true →
    ∀ p : Prov, getProvider x.providers (specProvider x.spec) = some p →
      ∃ d : Driver, f x = Output.driver d ∧ d.name = p.name ∧
        d.model = specModel x.spec ∧ d.apiKeyEnv = provKeyEnv x.env p

/-- An insert after line 0 needs no anchor and always has a valid position,
also in an empty original. A list of one such op succeeds, applies one op,
reports "applied 1 op(s)", and lists no stale anchor. -/
def InsertAtTopSucceeds (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → ∀ op : Op, x.ops = [op] →
    op.kind = OpKind.insert → op.afterLine = 0 →
      (f x).ok = true ∧ (f x).appliedOps = 1 ∧ (f x).staleAnchors = [] ∧
        (f x).message = "applied 1 op(s)".toList

claims.law_text:
/-- "Refresh aggregate status from durable child rows (children own truth)."
The status of the batch row after the call does not depend on the child
summaries (`children`) or the task list (`tasks`) that the batch row holds.
Only the durable child rows decide it. -/
def ChildrenOwnTruth (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x y : Input) (j j' : Job),
    Legal x → Legal y →
    x.job = some j → y.job = some j' →
    y.store = x.store → y.parentCancelled = x.parentCancelled → y.now = x.now →

/-- "from Retry-After, unix epoch"
On 429, a Retry-After value of plain digits is a number of seconds from now.
The retry time is the clock plus that number, as a float sum. -/
def RetryAfterIsClockPlusSeconds (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x → is429 x = true → ∀ v,
    readH (normalize x.headers) retryAfterKeys = some v → digitsOnly v = true →
    ∃ s, f x = some s ∧
      s.retryAfterAt = some (fadd (clockOf x.now) (rnd (digitsVal v : Nat) 1))

/-- "One requests- or tokens-window snapshot."
A request window has the kind `requests`. When the request limit header has a
digit value, the window limit is the value of those digits. -/
def RequestWindowKindAndLimit (f : Impl) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Input, Legal x →
    (∀ s w, f x = some s → s.requests = some w → w.kind = "requests") ∧
    (∀ v, readH (normalize x.headers) requestLimitKeys = some v → digitsOnly v = true →
      ∃ s w, f x = some s ∧ s.requests = some w ∧ w.limit = some (digitsVal v))
